text:
Sam W: Morning y'all — sharing my new WFH corner because I'm proud and also slightly embarrassed. standing desk + cheap ring light, but my ISP had a weird outage this morning. anyone else seeing flakiness? pics below. https://i.imgur.com/abcd1234.jpg
Priya K: love the plant. :seedling: for flaky internet I'd try a quick router reboot and then check whether it's only one band. if you have an old ISP-supplied gateway, replace it — they throttle older firmware.
Tony L: nice setup! I run Ubiquiti APs + a small Synology router. when I see jitter i do: ```ping -c 30 8.8.8.8``` and ```mtr 8.8.8.8``` to see where the packet loss is. If the loss is at the gateway -> call ISP.
Alex R: if it's home wiring, sometimes a bad splitter or old coax causes it. sounds dumb but unplug any extra splitters, test direct into the modem.
Sam W: thanks. rebooted modem & AP earlier and did ping -> avg 120ms which is wild for my area. filed a ticket with ISP. also ordered a small UPS for the modem so it doesn't go dark during brief brownouts.
Jess M: here's mine — cat approved keyboard hammock. warning: not ergonomic. https://i.imgur.com/catkeyboard.jpg :joy_cat:
Priya K: :laughing: also, if you want a cheap LTE backup, a USB dongle + basic policy routing on a cheap pfSense VM works well for failover. I keep one as a fallback for remote demos.
Tony L: if you want to keep latency low during failover, do sticky sessions by service IPs or use DNS-based failover with low TTLs. for quick testing, `iperf3` between two endpoints is great.
Alex R: small note — if you use VPN back to corp for everything, the VPN endpoint can become the bottleneck on failover. check that route counts.
Sam W: awesome tips, appreciate it. will try the `mtr` and maybe run `iperf3` later. bonus points if anyone has a recommendation for an unobtrusive desk mat (mine squeaks every time I move my mouse).
Priya K: Glorious desk mat, but the cork ones are quiet and look nicer than expected. :thumbsup:
Jess M: We should start a #wfh-setup thread with before/after pics. low effort, high morale.
Sam W: yes please. post your battle stations and any ISP horror stories. :coffee:
